quick.summary: Stop confusion by making one specific person responsible for a data set.
quick.takeaway: Assign an owner who creates the data to approve all changes.

beats.line: The total sales number changed again today. Who is supposed to fix it?
Think of a busy restaurant kitchen.
If everyone adds salt to the soup, it will taste terrible.
Your data is just like that soup. It needs a single head chef.
We call this establishing a stewardship framework.
Can I just say assigning a clear owner?
Exactly right. It needs one clear owner.
They set the rules, and they approve every single change.
That makes sense. But how do we pick the right owner?
You look for the person who creates the data.
Not the person who uses it the most?
No. The user only consumes it.
The creator knows where it came from and how it gets shaped.
So the sales manager owns the sales data.
If the marketing team wants to add a new column, they ask the owner.
The owner checks if the new column will break the report.
You got it. They protect the quality.

quiz.question: Who is usually the best person to own a specific data set?
options: The person who creates the data.
The team that requests the most reports.
The newest hire on the team.
Anyone who asks for permission first.
quiz.explanation: The creator understands the inputs and limitations of the data best, making them the ideal owner.

quiz.question: A data owner allows anyone to make changes to the data whenever they want.
quiz.explanation: The owner acts as a gatekeeper. They must approve changes to prevent errors from spreading.
